records.name: Norway
records.summary_text:
Norway is very safe for trans visitors, with strong legal protections and official responses, but with a more acute violence context than its Nordic neighbours. There is no criminalisation, bathrooms are unrestricted, and the Schengen border poses no trans-specific friction; anti-discrimination law covers gender identity; and the police operate a dedicated hate-crime unit with the security service providing annual Pride threat assessments.

records.name: Sweden
records.summary_text: Sweden is very safe. The one documented everyday-facility friction: a national swimming-pool chain's guidelines restrict trans persons' changing-room access — lawyers say this may violate discrimination law, so a trans visitor using such facilities may face exclusion. Brå (the crime-prevention council) reports roughly 6,700 LGBTQI-related hate-crime reports. Bathrooms as such are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation, and there is no rollback movement.
